findings.reason: without the declared dependency a coordinator can dispatch §4 in the same wave as §3 or before it, and the node's gate has no way to lower an estimate in which the anchor costs nothing.
findings.text: §8's text says "Section 4 follows section 3, since an opt-out is only meaningful once a mention is cheap enough", and §4's done-when at :137 requires the "same brief estimating lower with the opt-out than without it", yet the base charges a prose mention nothing (`_declared_input_files` at reckon/crew/routing.py:3177 collects only paths in a clause declaring them inputs, and the plan's own §3 comment at :277 says so), so §4's measure cannot hold unless §3's mention charge has landed — while no `plan-section-depends-on` meta declares s4 waits on s3 and both sections are declared `implementable` at :28

findings.reason: the now-dispatchable section states a root cause its own evidence contradicts, and a node sent to satisfy "charge a prose mention at a reference cost" would not be told that the census must first be widened to collect mentions that it currently never sees.
findings.text: the `reference-cost` decision is now locked at `flat`, which is the condition every earlier decline of the §3 findings said had to be met before those sections were revised and dispatched, but §3 (still `implementable` at :28) retains the premise the decision was to replace: "A path a node must edit and a path a node is told never to open are not the same load, and today they cost the same" (:112) and "it is currently the place it is most wrong" (:118) are both false against `_declared_input_files`, which does not see a path that appears only in prose at all, and the same section's done-when at :123-126 still asks a negated path that is "also a declared write path elsewhere" to be charged as a reference while "the write path must still be charged at full"
